The image shows corn stalks with dark brown to black discoloration on the rind. Key features: dark lesions coalescing into large dark blotches/streaks on the stalk surface, with a shiny black appearance. This is a stalk disease.

Top candidates: Anthracnose_stalk_rot, Bacterial_stalk_rot, Diplodia_stalk_rot, Physoderma_stalk_rot. Let me view references.

Initial prediction: **Anthracnose_stalk_rot** - the shiny dark brown to black discoloration on the stalk rind with lesions coalescing into large dark blotches is the hallmark symptom.

Let me check the attractor guide.
Anthracnose_stalk_rot is a known attractor. Let me check the key alternatives.

Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight shows leaf lesions and ear/husk symptoms - very different from the stalk rind discoloration in our test image. The other alternatives (Bacterial stalk rot, Diplodia stalk rot) were already viewed and don't match either.

The test image clearly shows the **distinctive shiny dark brown to black discoloration on the stalk rind** with dark lesions coalescing into large blotches/streaks along the internodes. This is the hallmark of Anthracnose stalk rot. No other stalk rot produces this characteristic shiny black rind appearance.

{"prediction": "Anthracnose_stalk_rot", "confidence": 0.82, "reasoning": "Stalks show distinctive shiny dark brown to black discoloration on the rind with lesions coalescing into large dark blotches and streaks along internodes - the hallmark symptom of anthracnose stalk rot. Distinguished from bacterial stalk rot (which shows water-soaked soft rot at nodes with collapse), Diplodia stalk rot (dry tan stalks with small black pycnidia), charcoal stalk rot (internal shredded pith with microsclerotia), and Physoderma stalk rot (black nodes specifically at first/second node)."}
